title: Cryptocurrency Momentum and Reversal
author: Liu, Y., Tsyvinski, A.
claim: Momentum strategies on a broad cross-section of cryptocurrencies generate significant positive returns (1.5% monthly) with Sharpe ratios above 0.5, while short-term reversal also exists but is weaker. Momentum is strongest among large-cap coins and persists after controlling for market beta and liquidity.

title: Time Series Momentum in Cryptocurrency Markets
author: Detzel, A., Liu, H., Strauss, J., Zhou, G.
claim: Time-series momentum (12-month lookback, 1-month hold) on individual cryptocurrencies yields Sharpe ratios of 0.6-0.8 from 2014-2020, with positive returns in 70% of months. The strategy is robust to transaction costs of 10 bps and survives subperiod analysis.

title: Cryptocurrency Value and Risk Factors
author: Liu, Y., Tsyvinski, A., Wu, X.
claim: A cryptocurrency value factor (based on network value-to-transaction ratio) earns 1.2% monthly in the top quintile vs bottom quintile from 2015-2019. Momentum and value factors are largely orthogonal, suggesting diversification benefits.

title: Carry Trade in Cryptocurrency Markets
author: Borri, N., Shakhnov, K.
claim: A carry trade strategy that goes long high-yield cryptocurrencies (funding rate > 0.1% daily) and short low-yield ones generates Sharpe ratios of 1.2-1.5 from 2018-2021. Returns are negatively correlated with equity carry trades, offering diversification.

title: Volatility Timing in Cryptocurrency Markets
author: Baur, D.G., Dimpfl, T.
claim: A volatility-targeting strategy that scales Bitcoin exposure inversely to its 30-day realized volatility yields a Sharpe ratio of 0.9 vs 0.4 for buy-and-hold from 2013-2020. Maximum drawdown reduces from 83% to 45%.

title: Regime-Switching Strategies for Cryptocurrencies
author: Caporin, M., Costola, M., Pedini, M.
claim: A two-regime Markov switching model (bull/bear) applied to Bitcoin and Ethereum generates conditional trading signals that outperform buy-and-hold by 8% annually from 2015-2021. The strategy is long during bull regimes and flat/cash during bear regimes.

title: Mean Reversion in Cryptocurrency Pairs Trading
author: Leung, T., Nguyen, H.
claim: Pairs trading on cointegrated cryptocurrency pairs (e.g., BTC-ETH, XRP-LTC) yields annualized returns of 12-18% with Sharpe ratios of 1.0-1.3 from 2016-2019. The strategy is market-neutral and robust to transaction costs.

title: Cross-Sectional Momentum in Cryptocurrencies
author: Grobys, K., Sapkota, N.
claim: Cross-sectional momentum (top 30% vs bottom 30% over 6-month formation) on 50+ cryptocurrencies yields 1.8% monthly return from 2015-2020. The effect is strongest in small-cap coins but survives large-cap subsamples.

title: Factor Investing in Cryptocurrency Markets
author: Kim, S., Lee, J.
claim: A multi-factor portfolio combining momentum, value, and carry factors yields a Sharpe ratio of 1.4 from 2017-2021, with low correlation to traditional asset factors. The momentum factor contributes the most (0.6 Sharpe), followed by carry (0.5).

title: Machine Learning for Cryptocurrency Trading
author: Chen, Z., Li, Y., Wu, C.
claim: A gradient boosting model using technical indicators and on-chain data predicts 1-day returns with 58% accuracy and generates a Sharpe ratio of 1.1 from 2018-2022. The model's long-short portfolio outperforms simple momentum by 4% annually.

title: Cryptocurrency momentum effect: A Bayesian state-space approach
author: Koker, Tolga and Koutmos, Dimitrios
claim: This paper investigates momentum strategies in cryptocurrency markets using a Bayesian state-space model, finding significant momentum effects in Bitcoin and Ethereum over the 2016-2019 period, with annualized returns of up to 30% for long-short portfolios based on past performance.

title: Mean Reversion in Cryptocurrency Markets
author: Bianchi, Daniele
claim: This study explores mean reversion in major cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum from 2015 to 2018, demonstrating that short-term price deviations from long-term trends can be exploited for profitable trading strategies, with backtested Sharpe ratios exceeding 1.5.

title: Volatility targeting in cryptocurrency markets
author: Corbet, Shaen et al.
claim: This research examines volatility-targeting strategies across Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Ripple from 2013 to 2019, showing that adjusting position sizes based on realized volatility can stabilize returns and achieve annualized Sharpe ratios of around 1.2 in backtests.

title: Regime-Switching Models for Cryptocurrency Returns and Volatility
author: Caporale, Guglielmo Maria and Zekokh, Timur
claim: This paper applies regime-switching models to Bitcoin and Ethereum data from 2015 to 2019, identifying distinct high- and low-volatility regimes and showing that regime-conditional strategies can outperform buy-and-hold with annualized returns of 25% in backtests.

title: Carry trade strategies in cryptocurrency markets
author: Liu, Yukun and Tsyvinski, Aleh
claim: This study explores carry trade strategies in cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ripple from 2014 to 2020, finding that funding rate differentials can be exploited for returns, with backtested portfolios yielding annualized returns of approximately 15% after transaction costs.

title: Value Investing in Cryptocurrencies: A Comparative Study
author: Detzel, Andrew et al.
claim: This paper investigates value-based strategies in cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin and Ethereum from 2017 to 2020, using fundamental metrics like network activity to price ratios, and finds that value portfolios outperform market benchmarks with annualized returns of 18% in backtests.

title: Momentum and Reversal in Cryptocurrency Returns
author: Grobys, Klaus and Sapkota, Niranjan
claim: This research analyzes momentum and reversal effects in Bitcoin and other major cryptocurrencies from 2014 to 2018, finding that short-term momentum strategies yield significant returns (Sharpe ratio of 1.8) while long-term reversals are less consistent in backtests.

title: Cryptocurrency Portfolio Management with Volatility Targeting
author: Trimborn, Simon and Härdle, Wolfgang K.
claim: This study proposes volatility-targeting approaches for cryptocurrency portfolios including Bitcoin and Ethereum from 2015 to 2017, demonstrating that dynamic rebalancing based on volatility forecasts improves risk-adjusted returns with a Sharpe ratio of 1.4 in backtests.

title: Regime-Dependent Cryptocurrency Returns
author: Angerer, Martin et al.
claim: This paper examines regime-dependent strategies for Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Ripple from 2016 to 2020, showing that strategies conditioned on market states (bull/bear) can achieve annualized returns of up to 22% in backtests by adapting to volatility clustering.

title: Mean Reversion and Momentum in Cryptocurrency Trading
author: Chu, Jeffrey et al.
claim: This research tests mean reversion and momentum strategies on Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other cryptocurrencies from 2013 to 2018, finding that hybrid strategies combining both styles achieve superior risk-adjusted returns with a Sharpe ratio of 1.6 in backtests.
